outcome: Healthcare resource use (Caesarean delivery rates, length of stay, cost of birth admission, midwifery-in-the-home visits)
cohort: Pregnant women attending publicly funded antenatal outpatient clinics in Newcastle, Australia
finding: Higher pre-pregnancy BMI was associated with increased odds of caesarean delivery and higher birth admission costs, while higher ARFS was associated with a small reduction in maternal length of stay, but not with mode of delivery or midwifery-in-the-home visits.
mod_finding: Higher pre-pregnancy BMI was associated with increased odds of caesarean delivery.
